title: Accounts API
context: First version of the accounts API used by the mobile app: list accounts and withdraw cash.

issues.title: No authorisation
issues.why: Any caller can withdraw from any account id, and GET /accounts returns every customer's account.
issues.fix: Take the user from the security context and check they own the account.

issues.title: Lost update, no rules, logic in the controller
issues.why: Read, change and save with no transaction or lock: two withdrawals at once can both pass. Nothing stops negative amounts or overdrafts.
issues.fix: Move it into a @Transactional service method with locking (a @Version column or SELECT … FOR UPDATE) and validate the amount and balance.

issues.title: Floating point used for money
issues.why: Floating point can't represent most decimal amounts exactly, so balances drift by fractions of a cent.
issues.fix: Use BigDecimal (or long minor units) end to end.

issues.title: JPA entity returned from the API
issues.why: It exposes every internal field, ties the API contract to the DB schema, and can trigger lazy-loading errors during serialisation.

issues.title: Unbounded query
issues.why: Loads every account into memory in one response.
issues.fix: Paginate (Pageable) and filter to the caller's own accounts.

issues.title: Optional.get() gives a 500 instead of a 404
issues.why: A missing id throws NoSuchElementException, which the catch-all handler turns into a confusing response.

fix.java: Use orElseThrow with a not-found exception mapped to 404.
fix.kotlin: Use findByIdOrNull(id) ?: throw a not-found exception mapped to 404.

issues.title: Catch-all handler returns 200 and leaks details
issues.why: Every error comes back as HTTP 200 with the raw exception message, so clients think it worked and internals leak.
issues.fix: Use a @RestControllerAdvice that maps exceptions to proper status codes with a ProblemDetail body, and log server errors.

why.java: Hides dependencies, prevents final fields, and makes unit tests need reflection or a Spring context.
why.kotlin: lateinit field injection hides dependencies, allows a mutable public property, and makes unit tests need a Spring context.

fix.java: Use constructor injection with a private final field.
fix.kotlin: Use constructor injection: class AccountController(private val accountRepository: AccountRepository).
